    • FX MORNING NOTES

    GS FX Research Notes: BRL Takes A Strong Signal From The First Round

    Research | Economics | 5 October 2026 | 8:24AM UTC

    Senator Flávio Bolsonaro won a stronger-than-expected 47.1% of valid votes, significantly outperforming the latest polls, whereas incumbent President Lula secured 45.1% of votes. Pro-Bolsonaro and right-of-centre candidates generally outperformed expectations in Senate and gubernatorial races. See our economists’ take on the results here.

    Ahead of the election, we argued that first-round results could provide meaningful information to market participants and drive a large FX market response, especially as BRL performance heading into the first round had been more range-bound than in prior elections. While this range-bound performance meant BRL already outperformed other LatAm currencies over the past week, we have found this to be more a reflection of underperformance relative to fundamentals elsewhere, whereas BRL continued to trade closely with its typical beta to global market developments.

    Futures currently point to an ~4% move lower in USD/BRL, which would be similar to the move on the Monday following the first round of the 2022 election (chart below). Around the 2018 election window, when Jair Bolsonaro was elected, USD/BRL moved ~10% lower. The Real continued to appreciate following the first round, before reaching its strongest levels on the Friday prior to the second round. This benchmark would imply the Real could appreciate further from here. In 2018, as the second round approached, focus turned swiftly to reform implementation amid a divided Congress. Governability concerns may be less acute this time around, but given the highly challenging fiscal backdrop we still expect policy announcements to gain greater importance as we get closer to and through the second round.

    Ahead of the second round, we will be focused on how votes for other candidates are re-allocated (though a substantial degree of voter migration to the main two candidates already took place) as well as any policy or personnel announcements from the two candidates, and how these may impact polling for the second round.

    More broadly, we see 4.50-4.80 as a plausible range for USD/BRL under an election outcome that is perceived as market-friendly and conducive to a tighter fiscal stance. In particular, trading at 4.80 would be consistent with the 'residual' fiscal premium from the 2024 BRL depreciation episode fully compressing as well as longer-run valuations. The Real could appreciate beyond these levels if fiscal consolidation efforts justify a 'positive' fiscal premium and if the external backdrop is also supportive for BRL.

    Chart of the Day. USD/BRL performance into the first round had been more range-bound than in prior elections, but the implied move today would be similar to that in the 2022 election cycle.
